parts.name: bracket
parts.note: The SDK bracket (et-bracket) in flow, first drawing, drawn by the mock from @ethlete/components/design/bracket with the real markup and CSS: the bracket, its default round header, default match cell (et-match-card at compact), default final card (trophy, round name, champion line), continue cell and participants legend sheets, plus the match card, icon and button sheets; cell positions and connector paths come from @ethlete/bracket (createBracket, the single elimination grid, drawMan) as in the lib; default settings and labels, en-US kick-off. Emblems are the participant's letter fallback; the move transitions at rest. Fixtures are fictional: an eight-club single elimination knockout (Northbridge Rovers NBR 1, Harbor City HBC 2, Eastvale United EVU 3, Millbrook Athletic MBA 4, Riverside Wanderers RSW 5, Stonegate FC SGF 6, Westport Albion WPA 7, Lakeside Town LST 8) over Quarter-finals, Semi-finals and Final; the brand theme only. Framed as a page with 16px padding at 1040 and 1680 (the default bracket is 980px wide, the grid does not follow the frame width). States: in-progress (quarter-finals and one semi-final finished, the other semi-final live 1 : 1 with the LIVE badge, the final with Northbridge Rovers against TBD and the kick-off, champion not decided), decided (Westport Albion beat Northbridge Rovers 2 : 1, the champion line), journey-hover (the hover journey of Riverside Wanderers: the rest at half opacity, the semi-final where they went out dashed and their row struck through), journey-pinned (the pinned journey of the champion with the participants legend, its toggle pressed; the rest at a quarter opacity), legend-focus-visible (the Eastvale United toggle forced), compact (density compact, in-progress), continue (quarter-finals and semi-finals with the continue cell, 2 winners advance, dashed connectors) and mirrored (decided, folded in half, compact, so it fits 1040). Numbers (light / dark), from shot pixels at scale 2 at 1040, brand mint, a: winner bar (primary) vs card 1.33 / 13.50; live dot (primary) vs its badge tint 1.24 / 9.67, vs card 1.33 / 13.28; badge tint vs card 1.07 / 1.37; final frame edge (45 % mint) vs page 1.22 / 3.90, vs the glow beside it 1.15 / 2.98, vs its own tint 1.18 / 3.50; the final tint (6 %) vs page 1.03 / 1.11; pressed legend toggle (mint fill) vs page 1.33 / 13.50, its label 15.82 / 15.82; legend toggle focus ring (primary) vs page 1.37 / 13.06; outline toggle edge and label (ink) 7.68 light. Q98 numbers only: connectors, card edges, the continue cell's dashed edge and the journey endpoint's dashed outline vs page 1.26 / 1.73. The journey dimming lowers text under 4.5:1 by design: at half opacity the check reports a dimmed winner code at 3.41 / 2.68 and the dimmed Final label at 2.14 / 3.93, at a quarter opacity 1.73 / 2.21, the struck-through row that went out (0.55 opacity) 2.62 / 2.98; exempted with contrast exceptions, an open point, no decided rule. Decided rules that arise: Q88 (the legend toggle focus ring; the default cells are not links, so no card ring) and Q99a (the winner bar, the live dot and the final frame edge take ink in light; the pressed legend toggle is a mint fill, so it takes a 1px inset ink edge). The ink edge on a mint fill arises, so Q102 arises: b draws the edge in both schemes, c keeps dark as today (light-dark(ink, transparent)). The badge tint and the final tint are band tints, not fills, so they are kept, and the final glow is kept. Q101 does not arise: the only filled button is a pressed toggle, whose hover keeps the fill in the lib. Findings for later: (1) lib bug: the live meta row grows the bracket's compact card past matchHeight: the live semi-final is 87px tall in its 75px cell (65 in 52 at compact), so it hangs 12px (13px) below its cell, the incoming connector meets it 6px above its centre and the gap to the card below shrinks. Drawn as is in every variant. (2) In the mirrored compact layout the final card in its 200px column shows full names and cuts the loser ('Northbridge Rove…') next to the score, where every other compact cell shows codes. (3) The eliminated row's line-through also strikes the emblem letter and the score. (4) The lit journey path keeps the grey connector colour (1.26 / 1.73), so it reads only by the rest fading; the dimmed text is under 4.5:1 (numbers above). (5) In dark the final glow lightens the page beside the frame edge, so the edge drops from 3.90 against the bare page to 2.98 against the glow. Later rounds, left out here: double elimination, swiss and round robin layouts, the third-place match, the mirrored layout at default density, the rounds list and adaptive layout, the skeleton, the prediction pick card, a custom match component on a link (card hover and focus ring), emblems as images, scheduled cells with kick-off times, long names, RTL and the move transitions. Omitted option value (Q182): alignRoundHeaders center draws the same pixels as start, because the default round header fills its column and is already centred.

parts.name: chart
parts.note: The SDK charts (et-bar-chart, et-line-chart, et-pie-chart), first drawing, drawn by their mocks from @ethlete/components/design/chart with the real markup and CSS: bar, line and pie chart sheets plus the axis, grid, legend, chart tooltip and line chart tooltip sheets, and the et-tooltip pane for the open tooltip. Framed as a 480px page with 16px padding; bar and line plots 410px wide, 240px high (the default); pie 200px (the default), donut innerRadius 0.6 with its total. Single series draw in the accent; two or more in accent mix steps (100 / 40 %, pie 100 / 80 / 60 / 40 %). States: bar (Jan to Jun), bar-series (2025 and 2026, legend), bar-hover and bar-focus-visible (Apr), bar-tooltip (Mar 2025, hover with its tooltip), bar-empty (projected etBarChartEmpty text), bar-long-label (January 2026 ... June 2026: the auto label spacing thins to every second label); line, line-series (Visits and Sign-ups, legend), line-points, line-hover and line-focus-visible (Thu: crosshair, slice dots, focus box), line-tooltip (Wed, active slice with the multi-series tooltip); pie, donut, pie-hover and pie-focus-visible (Search), pie-tooltip (Direct), pie-empty (all zero: the empty ring), pie-long-label (a long legend label, ellipsed). Static snapshot: the bar grow, line reveal and slice fade are drawn at rest. The lib has no loading state. Numbers (light / dark), from shot pixels at scale 2, brand mint, a: mint marks (bars, line 1, dots, legend and tooltip keys) 1.33 / 13.50; 40 % series (bar 2026, line 2) 1.13 / 2.79; axis and legend text (muted) 7.81 / 6.94; crosshair (subtle) 4.95 / 4.99; hover and focus tint 1.07 / 1.08; focus rings: bar and line (2px, series colour / primary) 1.33 / 13.50, pie (2px, text colour) 17.93 / 17.18. Q98 numbers only: grid lines vs page 1.26 / 1.73 (as the table's edges). Decided rules that arise: Q88 (bar, line and pie focus rings), Q99a (on light the line strokes, slice dots, line legend swatches and tooltip keys take ink in their mix steps; bars, pie slices and the square legend swatches are mint fills and get a 1px ink edge). Series colours otherwise stay data colours: the mix steps are kept. Q101 does not arise: no filled button. An ink edge arises, so Q102 arises: under the brand theme the dark ink is the mint, so the edge is invisible on the full mint fill but shows as a bright outline around the 40 % series in dark (b), while c drops it there. The thinned first and last category labels sit inside the plot (lib fix 3c26c2204). Findings for later, not render refusals: the pie focus ring in b is the same ink as its new 1px edge, only 1px wider, so a focused slice reads close to rest (a used the text colour); d draws it as an outer ring instead. The pie tooltip opens over the legend. Later rounds, left out here: horizontal and stacked bars, negative values, area and stacked area, the time scale, sankey, per-series colour themes, the title and note slots, touch tap.

parts.name: checkbox
parts.note: The SDK checkbox (et-checkbox) in flow, first drawing, drawn by the mock from @ethlete/components/design/checkbox with the real markup and CSS: et-checkbox alone and inside et-choice-field (label, et-description, hint, error, required marker), the card variant (et-selection-card), and et-checkbox-group with et-checkbox-group-select-all and et-checkbox-option, plus the color-interactive and focus-ring sheets; the brand theme, danger as the error theme. Fixtures are fictional: a match-report preferences form (Send me the match report, One email per match, no ads., hint We send it after the final whistle.; I accept the terms of use, required, error Accept the terms to continue.; card Weekly digest, A summary of every match day, each Monday.; group Notify me about with All events over Kick-off, Goals, Half-time, Full-time; horizontal group Show matches: Home, Away, Neutral ground). Framed as a page with 16px padding at 360 and 640. States: a grid of unchecked, checked and indeterminate by rest, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled and readonly (all labelled); box-only (checked, no label); support (description and hint); invalid and invalid-focus-visible; card-rest, card-checked, card-hover, card-focus-visible, card-checked-focus-visible; group-unchecked, group-partial (2 of 4, select-all mixed), group-checked, group-option-hover, group-option-pressed (force hover and active), group-option-focus-visible, group-select-all-focus-visible and group-horizontal. Numbers (light / dark), from shot pixels at scale 2 at 360, brand mint, a: unchecked box border (surface border) vs page 1.26 / 1.73, the same for the option and select-all boxes and the card edge; hover border 10.37 / 13.07; checked and indeterminate fill (primary) vs page 1.33 / 13.50, check and dash on it 15.82; checked hover fill (-hover) 1.37 / 13.06, 1.03 from rest; active fill 2.24 / 8.01; focus-visible fill (-focus) 1.37 / 13.06; focus ring on a checked or indeterminate box (primary -focus) 1.37 / 13.06, on an unchecked box (surface text colour) 17.93 / 17.18; card checked edge and card ring (primary) 1.33 / 13.50; option and select-all ring 1.37 / 13.06; invalid box border (danger) 4.83 / 3.71, its focus ring (danger -focus) 6.47 / 2.77; disabled checked fill 2.20 / 1.70, disabled unchecked border 1.12 / 1.27 (exempt under 1.4.11). Decided rules that arise: Q88 (the checked and indeterminate ring, the invalid ring, the card ring, the option and select-all rings in ink; the unchecked ring is the surface text colour, not a primary ring, so it stays), Q99a (the card checked and focus edge and the focused option, select-all and card box borders take light-dark(ink, primary); the checked and indeterminate box, the checked option box and the checked or mixed select-all box are mint fills, so they take a 1px inset ink edge, an outline at -1px as in the table round; on the option and select-all the focus ring owns the outline, so the edge leaves while it shows) and Q101 (a filled checked or indeterminate box hovers to -active). The ink edge on a mint fill arises, so Q102 arises: b draws the edges in both schemes, c keeps dark as today (light-dark(ink, transparent)). The error border is the danger theme, not mint, and passes 3:1, so it is kept. Findings for later: (1) lib bug: .et-checkbox-box, .et-checkbox-option-box and .et-checkbox-group-select-all-box were content-box, so --et-checkbox-size 20px drew a 24px box (48 sheet px at scale 2) in an app without a global border-box reset, and the hint and error started 4px left of the label column. Fixed in the lib (box-sizing: border-box on the three boxes): every box draws 20px (40 sheet px), and the label, description and hint share one column (44 CSS px from the frame edge). (2) WCAG 1.4.11: the unchecked box border is 1.26 / 1.73 vs page, under 3:1; it is the only edge of an unchecked box (the same question as the switch off track, switch r1, open). Not drawn. (3) The required marker takes the error theme primary: 3.71:1 in dark, under 4.5:1; exempted here. (4) Focus-visible lightens the checked fill to -focus (1.37 vs page, light), so a focused checked box reads paler than at rest; the ink ring carries the state in b and c. (5) Readonly draws exactly like rest (no affordance by design); a checked readonly box cannot be told from an editable one. (6) Mock: et-description now has its own stylesheet (description.component.css, f5722a1f5), so the mock's inline copy can import it instead. Later rounds, left out here: the sizes sm and lg, the card with the control at start, a coloured (non-brand) checkbox, the group's bulk-edit mixed state (dashed option boxes, a primary mark that Q99a would reach), a disabled or readonly group, a group with error and the group card variant, long labels that wrap, RTL and the check and uncheck animation.

parts.note: The SDK otp input (et-otp-input), first drawing, drawn by the mock from @ethlete/components/design/otp-input with the real markup and CSS: et-label with the required marker, the segment row, the invisible native input over it, et-form-support with hint and error; the brand theme, danger as the error theme. The field has no :focus or :hover CSS of its own: focus is the data-caret segment (a 1px border plus a 1px inset outline in primary, and a blinking 2px caret bar in an empty one), which the mock draws with focused. Fixtures are fictional: Verification code, 6 digits 482193, hint We sent it to +49 151 0000 0000., required with error Enter the code from the SMS.; a 4-digit masked PIN. Framed as a page with 16px padding at 320, 360 and 640. States: empty, partial, filled, hover, focus-empty, focus-partial, focus-filled, hint, required, invalid, invalid-partial, invalid-focus, disabled, disabled-filled, readonly, readonly-focus, pin-partial and pin-focus. Numbers (light / dark), from shot pixels at scale 2 at 360, brand mint, a: segment 44px outer (border-box, fixed in 00072d935), gap 8px, row 304px, digits 19.8px; empty and filled segment border (surface border) vs page 1.26 / 1.73, the only edge of a segment; caret segment edge and caret bar (primary) 1.33 / 13.50; required marker (brand primary) 1.33 / 13.50; invalid border (danger) 4.83 / 3.71; label (muted) 7.81 / 6.94; disabled digits 2.55 / 3.72 (opacity 0.4, exempt). Decided rules that arise: Q88 (focus in ink: the caret segment edge and the caret bar take ink, the invalid one the danger ink) and Q99a (a mint mark on light takes ink: the required marker light-dark(ink, primary)). Hover follows the text field (form-field-text-shell: the frame border to surface-interaction-hover, the error frame to ink, none when readonly or disabled), on the host since the host is the click target (otp.activate()). The filled segment edge in c is my proposal, not a decided rule (Q103). Findings for later, lib bugs apart: (L1) a 6-digit field needed 304px and never shrank; at 320 with 16px page padding it overflowed by 16px (drawn at 320). Now fixed: the segments shrink, 41.3px at 320, and the render at 640 is unchanged. (L2) a readonly field showed the focus caret segment and, when not full, the blinking caret bar, though nothing can be typed (readonly-focus). Now fixed: no caret when readonly. Design: (1) WCAG 1.4.11: the segment border 1.26 / 1.73 is the only edge of an empty segment, as with the checkbox box and the radio circle. Not drawn. (2) A filled segment looks like an empty one apart from its digit; c answers it. (3) The error border is the full danger primary, while the text field draws its error frame at 50 % danger; kept, it passes 3:1. (4) Hover (10.37 / 13.07) outshines the focus edge (5.48 / 13.50) in b and c, as it does on the text field. (5) The masked dot is a 19.8px bullet, about 5px wide. (6) The error marker 3.71 in dark, exempted as in checkbox r1. Later rounds, left out here: data-warning (no CSS of its own), a coloured field, alphanumeric codes, other lengths and segment sizes via the custom properties, RTL and the pop-in animation.

The time grid draws 8:00 to 18:00 as if the scrolling body sat on that window, with business hours 9 to 17 on weekdays and the weekend outside them; the current time line sits on today at 11:15. Framed as a page with 16px padding. Widths 560, 800 and 1200 (all above the 480px container width where the header switches to floating action buttons). States: week, week-dragging (Retro lifted, with the drag shadow), appointment-hover, appointment-focus-visible (Daily sync on Monday forced), slot-focus-visible (Thursday 11:00 forced), day, month (outside-month days, today, a +3 more trigger, the selected appointment), month-cell-focus-visible, agenda (a month heading, today, nested rows with tree guides, the selected appointment). Numbers (light / dark), from shot pixels at scale 2 at 800, brand mint, a: appointment tint (14 %) vs page 1.07 / 1.37, its title ink on it 5.12 / 9.84; selected appointment (mint fill) vs page 1.33 / 13.50, its text 15.82 / 15.82; today date circle (mint fill) vs page 1.33 / 13.50, its digit 15.82; current time line and its dot vs the today column 1.29 / 12.14; focus ring (primary) vs page 1.35 / 13.50, vs the appointment tint 1.26 / 9.84; Add appointment fill vs page 1.33 / 13.50, its label 15.82. Q98 numbers only: grid lines (hour rows, day columns, header and all-day edges, month cells) vs page 1.26 / 1.73; the non-business band 1.07 / 1.08; the today column tint is 6 % mint. Decided rules that arise: Q88 (every focus ring: slots, all-day cells, month cells, appointments, the overflow trigger, the view switch, the header buttons), Q99a (the current time line and its dot, the appointment color dot; the selected appointment, the today date circles and the filled Add appointment button are mint fills, so they take a 1px inset ink edge) and Q101 (the filled button hover = -active). The ink edge on a mint fill arises, so Q102 arises: b draws the edges in both schemes, c keeps dark as today (light-dark(ink, transparent)). The 32 / 38 / 44 % selection step does not arise: a selected appointment is a solid mint fill, not a tint. Findings for later: (1) lib bug: the badge pieces render inside their component hosts (et-scheduler-badge-color-dot, -title, -time-range, -location, -chain-count), which are inline, so the flex rules on the inner spans never apply: the color dot is 0 x 0 and never shows (also in Storybook), the title does not take flex: 1 or ellipsis, and the time range and location are cut hard at the block edge (the agenda location shrinks to one letter while the title has room). Fixed in the lib (display: contents on the five hosts; the time range and location shrink with an ellipsis before the title). Narrow week blocks still clip, because the gaps, the dot and the chain count alone are wider than the block (31 px at 560), so data-et-skip CLIPPED stays on every time grid block; the month cell skip is gone. (2) The first hour label sat half above the scroll body (translateY(-50%)) and was clipped by its overflow; fixed in the lib with a top padding of half the label line height. (3) Outside-month dates read nearly like in-month ones. (4) The selected appointment edge and the drag shadow share box-shadow, so a selected appointment being dragged would lose one (not drawn); the lib has no selected edge yet, so whoever merges b or c must list the edge and the drag shadow in one rule on [data-selected][data-dragging]. (5) The Add appointment hover (Q101) is not forced here; it is the same et-button as in the stream round (hover 1.69 from rest). Later rounds, left out here: the edit surface (scheduler-edit-surface and its parts, an overlay), the month +n more menu, the narrow header with floating action buttons, the drag-to-create draft and committed blocks, month draft and drop-target cells, the scrollbar, custom badge adornments, the read-only scheduler, RTL and long labels.

parts.name: slider
parts.note: The SDK slider (et-slider) and range slider (et-range-slider), first drawing, drawn by slider() from @ethlete/components/design/slider with the real markup and CSS: et-label with the required marker, the interaction box with rail, fill, ticks with and without labels, one or two thumbs with the value bubble an etSliderThumbLabel template renders, et-form-support with hint and error; the brand theme, danger as the error theme. Hover, focus-visible and active are forced on a thumb, dragging as data-dragging on the host and thumb. Fixtures are fictional: Volume 0-100 at 0, 40 and 100, hint Applies to match highlights only., required at 95 with error Keep the volume at 80 or below.; steps of 10 with and without ticks; Quality with Low, Medium, High; Price range 20-80, 0-100, met at 50, in steps of 20 EUR; mixed with Different volumes, hint The selected clips disagree.; vertical with a value bubble and with labelled ticks; an unlabelled slider. Framed as a page with 16px padding at 320, 360 and 640. Numbers (light / dark), from shot pixels at scale 2 at 360, brand mint, a: rail (32 % surface-interaction) vs page 1.51 / 1.81; fill and thumb (primary) 1.33 / 13.50, thumb vs rail 1.14 / 7.45; focus ring (primary) 1.33 / 13.50; disabled (opacity 0.4) thumb 1.19 / 3.09, rail 1.18 / 1.22; thumb 18px, no border, so box-sizing does not change its size; the interaction box is 44px tall and the full track width on et-slider, so the touch target passes there; the thumb at min and max stays inside the host (margin-inline half a thumb) and lines up its outer edge with the label. Hover, active and dragging draw exactly like rest; readonly draws exactly like rest; invalid only turns the fill and thumb danger. Decided rules that arise: Q88 (the focus ring in ink; the invalid one takes the danger ink), Q99a (the mint fill and the mixed dashed rail take light-dark(ink, primary), the mint thumb keeps a 1px inset ink edge, the required marker light-dark(ink, primary)) and Q101 (a thumb hovers and drags to -active). No et-description on the slider, so form-field L1 does not arise. Lib bugs apart, all four fixed in the lib since: (S1) the value bubble overlapped et-label: nothing reserved room above the interaction box (Storybook Range Slider Default with showValueLabel at 360: bubble y 33.8-56.6, label y 42-57.6, the 20 bubble cut Price range; Slider Value Label: bubble y 41.8-64.6 over the label row). Fixed: a host with a value label carries data-thumb-value and gives the interaction box a 17.8px block-start margin (bubble y 59.6-82.4, label ends at 57.6); the 18px b and c draw replaces it, it does not add up. (S2) et-range-slider had a 28px interaction box, et-slider 44px (Storybook: h 28.0 vs 44.0). Fixed: both 44px, the range slider grows by 16px; b and c set the same 44px. (S3) vertical tick labels hung outside the host on the inline-start side (Storybook Vertical Marks at 360: host x 42, Medium x 11, High x 27, Low x 29). Fixed: the labels take a column as wide as the longest label, inside the host (Medium x 42); the 32px inline-start margin b and c drew doubled up with it and is gone. (S4, minor) the bubble and tick label on an end tick centred on it and overhung the host (Range Slider Labelled Marks: first label x 29, host x 42; range-ends: the 0 bubble left of the host). Fixed: their translate clamps at the track ends, so both start at the host edge (x 42). Design: (1) WCAG 1.4.11: the rail 1.51 / 1.81 is the only edge of the unfilled track; c draws it in surface-interaction, 4.74 / 6.94, but in light the ink fill then sits at 1.16 against it, told apart by hue only. (2) No hover, pressed or dragging look in a; Q101 in b shifts the thumb to -active, barely visible on an 18px thumb; c adds a 6px primary halo at 28 % while pressed or dragged (my proposal). (3) Readonly looks exactly like an editable slider and keeps focus; c draws a ring thumb in the page colour with a 2px light-dark(ink, primary) border (my proposal, box-sizing set). (4) On the ink fill of b and c the active ticks (on-primary at 70 %) sit near 3.0 against it, weaker than on the mint. (5) The error required marker takes the error theme primary, 3.71:1 in dark; Q113: it is not exempt and needs 4.5:1, drawn as is in this round. (6) Invalid has no mark beyond the danger colour of fill and thumb. Later rounds, left out here: thumb size tokens, the colour themes besides brand, RTL, the dragging motion and the bubble on focus only.

parts.name: title-bar
parts.note: The window title bar: a compact 32 px drag region on the app background, closed off from the content below by a 1 px bottom border. The centred search field (components/title-search) names the product and part you are in and draws its own states. Update, a filled brand button, shows only when an update is ready and ends the bar before the window controls. macOS reserves 78 px left for the native traffic lights (drawn as three neutral grey dots, like an inactive window); Linux draws round buttons on the side its button layout gives; Windows draws square tiles with a red close hover. The grid draws each control at rest, hovered, pressed and focused: Update (linux-full-update), minimize (linux-left), the round close (linux-close), maximize (windows) and the square close (windows-update).

parts.name: title-search
parts.note: The search field in the window title bar: a wide tonal field that names the product and part you are in and opens the command palette (click or Ctrl K / ⌘ K). Search icon, product name and shortcut are muted at rest and take the full surface text colour when hovered, pressed or focused; the product name is always whole; a part name too long for the field ends in an ellipsis and the label then starts at the left instead of the centre. Each row draws the field at rest, hovered, pressed and focused; the long row cuts the part name off with an ellipsis and shows the macOS shortcut.

parts.note: The SDK tooltip, drawn by its mock from @ethlete/components/design: the open pane with its arrow on the inherited surface. Short text, long text that wraps at the 34ch max width, template content, and each side the pane opens on, plus a -start and an -end placement with the arrow 20 px in. In the dark scheme the pane border and the arrow edge are a 1 px ring in --et-surface-ring-solid, 24 % --et-surface-color-solid over the fill, as in the foundations/elevation round. The token is defined here; the generator does not emit it yet.

parts.name: tree
parts.note: The SDK tree, drawn by its mock from @ethlete/components/design. Rows keep a roving tab stop, so a focused row draws the real :focus-visible ring.

parts.name: tree-row
parts.note: One mark family: every end mark is a 12px line icon with the same stroke, its detail in a tooltip. Interaction is a background fill: hover lays the raised surface under the row, selection an accent tint with accent text, selected and hovered stacks both, pressed lays a fill a step darker than hover (a selected row keeps its hover tint), and focus-visible draws an inset ring. The stack has no outer padding; the host sets it.

parts.name: update-dialog
parts.note: Confirm before the Update button restarts Studio: an anchored dialog under the Update button, arrow pointing at it, no scrim. "Später" only closes it; the Update button stays.

parts.name: zoom-chip
parts.note: The zoom chip in the canvas corner: zoom out, the zoom in percent (resets to 100 %), zoom in, fit. Each row draws one button at rest, hovered, pressed and focused, at 25 %, 100 % or 250 %. The root has `data-canvas-zoom`; each button sits in a `data-camera-out`, `-reset`, `-in` or `-fit` wrapper for a setup to wire. A host places it through `class`, for example `absolute right-space-3 bottom-space-3`.

parts.name: canvas-frames
parts.note: The frames of one part on the canvas, in the state grid look: a sunken frame body, the cells as one component sheet with hairline dividers, labels outside the sheet. A click selects a frame (a 2 px primary outline), a second click on the selected frame, the double click, makes it live (a dashed outline and the Live · Esc badge in its head; Escape leaves it). A frame keeps following the size of its content; it has no size control. A frame whose page failed to load shows the reason and Neu laden on top of it. On the variant grid each round has a head: its title folds the round to one narrow column with its note, the switch beside it shows the unchanged states; a column head names the variant above its frames. The element also exports that look (stateGrid, canvasFrameHead, canvasFrameBox, canvasFrame, canvasView, canvasFrameStyles) for pages that draw their own frames; canvasView places components/zoom-chip in the corner. It fills its container and leaves room for a side panel through --st-shell-inset-left.

parts.name: part-tree
parts.note: A dense, quiet tree of the product parts: layers, then parts, then the frames of an open part (a part drawn in one frame is a leaf), with a warning mark on a part that needs a look and no counts anywhere.

parts.name: shell-main
parts.note: The window title bar (components/title-bar) runs over the full window width, above rail and content, and names the product. The shell owns rail and panel geometry, with a 40-px studio slot for the independently composed Studio menu. Its standalone preview fills that slot with the neutral Studio mark; pages supply the complete menu element and its styles and setup. Menu states live on elements/studio-menu. Its layout states are panel open, panel hidden and project picker open, and the design server stopped and starting screens fill the content area with the server log and a restart button; the rail section and product buttons draw the shell hover fill, pressed fill and inset focus ring on --transition-state. The panel controls and their interaction states are their own parts: components/shell-collapse and components/shell-project-switch (the picker is its surface).

parts.name: studio-menu
parts.note: Studio-wide actions behind the neutral logo tile: the design server actions the server state allows (restart and stop while it runs, start while it is stopped). The element owns its trigger, SDK panel, styles, interaction states and prototype setup. Pages place its 40-px root in the shell rail slot.

parts.name: variant-cell
parts.note: One state of a sketch variant in the sketch matrix: the state name above, then the part drawn at its own width and scaled into the frame. A state the variant leaves as it was is dimmed and reads unverändert; the first state it changes carries erste Änderung. The host sets the frame width, the scale and the label size (`--sk-frame`, `--sk-scale`, `--sk-label`) and places the cell in its grid.

parts.name: flows
parts.note: Flows as a canvas with a page header: a flat list of the flows in the side panel, the open flow name as the header title with the size picker at its right end, and the flow as a graph on a canvas with the sketch camera (pan by wheel and drag, zoom with the zoom chip in the corner; a flow starts at 100 % with its first frame at the left edge, below the header): frames in columns along the lines, a branch on its own row, every line an elbow arrow with its label above the last segment.

parts.name: inbox
parts.note: Inbox, flat: every thread of the product, newest first, in two groups: the part on the canvas on top, all others below, showing its latest message: mostly the exchange between the user and their AI agent (Claude, Codex and Gemini in this sample), plus a teammate QC pass. Each row has the author, the part and state it sits on, and a reply count. The canvas shows the frame of the selected comment with its pin. A click on a row, or Enter or Space on the focused row, selects its comment and opens its place on the canvas; for a comment on another part the canvas switches to that part first. States cover open comments only on the active part, an active part with no open comments, no open comments at all, the list while it loads, a load error with a retry, and a list longer than the panel, which scrolls. The comment editor is open only while focus is within it; moving focus between its controls keeps it open, and leaving the editor closes it.

parts.name: inventory
parts.note: The Inventory of a page, shown in place of the canvas when the Inventory toggle of a page is on: a header with the approval state, Reload and Approve inventory, the rest frames of the page with a numbered box on each control, and the numbered control list at the right with its status, kind and state count. An undeclared control is red, an unclassified one amber; Approve stays off while either is left.

parts.note: focus-visible nimmt --text wie hover

parts.name: sketches
parts.note: Eine Zeile je Variante, ganz oben Aktuell, bei einem neuen Teil ohne Aktuell und mit dem Badge neu. Links steht der Kopf: Variante, kurzer Modellname (Tooltip mit voller Kennung und Zeit), die Notiz und Übernehmen, das direkt die Merge-Ansicht öffnet; Übernehmen steht nur da, wenn der Sketch auf die Wahl wartet. Das Badge oben folgt dem echten Zustand: zeichnet, solange eine Variante gezeichnet wird, Wartet auf deine Wahl, wenn alle stehen, sonst Pausiert oder Keine Aktivität. Die Notiz wächst mit dem Zoom (15 px bei 100 %, nie unter 12 px bis Einpassen); weiter herausgezoomt skaliert der Kopf mit der Fläche, unter 9 px ist sein Text ausgeblendet. Rechts stehen die Zustände in einem Raster, jeder mit Namen (13 px mal Zoom, unter 9 px ausgeblendet). Ein Teil breiter als ein Viertel der Ansicht zeigt eine Matrix: eine Spalte je Variante, Aktuell zuerst, die Zustände als Zeilen, der Zustandsname einmal je Zeile links; beim Verschieben bleibt diese Spalte am linken Rand stehen. Einpassen nimmt Aktuell und die erste Variante, in der Matrix deren zwei Spalten; weitere erreicht man durch Verschieben. Solange der Vergleich läuft, sind alle Rahmen neutral und der Kopf zeigt vergleicht …; danach sind unveränderte Zustände gedimmt und der erste geänderte markiert. Varianten, die in jedem Zustand gleich Aktuell sind, liegen zusammen in einem zugeklappten Bereich unter den geänderten (in der Matrix eine schmale Spalte rechts), aufgeklappt wie vorher.

parts.name: start
parts.note: The start page before a product exists, without the shell: the section bubbles mean nothing without a product. Only the mark and a centred card in the same shape as the empty Flows and System pages. Without a repo the card asks to open a checkout; with a repo but no products it gives an example prompt for the agent, a copy button and the real CLI command.

parts.name: system
parts.note: The System page: the shell, a quiet collapsible tree of the product parts, and the infinite canvas. A product without parts shows a short line in the panel and a centred card on the canvas, the same card as the empty Flows page: a ghost of four boxes, a title, what the layers are, an example prompt for the agent and a copy button. Top right, beside the open-points chip, the Kommentar toggle turns comment mode on: each frame becomes a crosshair target, and a click opens a draft at that point with a text field, Abbrechen and Senden. While a comment is sent, the field and Abbrechen are disabled and Senden shows a spinner; a failed send keeps the text: a network or server error shows "Kommentar nicht gesendet. Erneut versuchen." under the field and turns Senden into Erneut senden; a send the server refuses with a 4xx shows the server reason there and keeps Senden, with no retry. The open-points popover also lists the exceptions of the part as an Ausnahmen group, each with its reason, state and a Freigeben button, and ends in a footer with Go geben (Go erteilt once given), or Änderung abnehmen for a direct edit of a merged part (Änderung abgenommen once done); the chip counts the exceptions with the points. A legacy call shows a header with its slug and headline, the surface and colour theme switches, and Als übertragen markieren, which turns into an übertragen badge.

rounds.note: Zurückgezogene Varianten sind standardmäßig ausgeblendet; die Runde zeigt drei Orte für den Schalter, der sie wieder zeigt.

a.note: Eintrag in der Rundenauswahl: Zurückgezogene zeigen (n). Kein neues Element in der Kopfzeile; kostet: der Schalter ist erst nach dem Öffnen der Auswahl sichtbar, und eine Rundenauswahl, die auch einen Filter umschaltet, mischt zwei Arten von Eintrag.

b.note: Kleiner Schalter Zurückgezogene (n) direkt neben der Rundenauswahl, nur wenn es eine gibt. Ohne Öffnen sichtbar, ein Klick, und der Schalter zeigt den Zustand an; kostet ein neues Bedienelement in der Kopfleiste, das neben der Auswahl mitgelesen werden muss.

c.note: Gedämpfte Fußzeile unter den Varianten: 1 zurückgezogen · anzeigen. Steht genau dort, wo die Variante fehlt, und nur wenn es eine gibt; kostet: in der Matrix und bei vielen Zuständen liegt sie weit unten und ist erst nach Verschieben sichtbar.
